learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how schools, hospitals, and NGOs keep track of their money when their main goal is helping society, not making a profit!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Organizations like clubs, charities, and public hospitals exist to provide services, not to earn profits. Because they don't have 'sales' or 'owners,' their accounting looks a bit different from regular businesses.

This is simply a summary of the Cash Book. It records all cash coming in (Receipts) and all cash going out (Payments) during the year, regardless of whether the money is for this year, last year, or next year.

This is the NPO version of a Profit & Loss Account. It only records income and expenses related strictly to the CURRENT year. Instead of Net Profit or Net Loss, the result is called 'Surplus' or 'Deficit'.

When someone donates money for a specific purpose (like a 'Building Fund' or 'Sports Fund'), that money cannot be used for anything else. It is kept in a separate fund on the Liabilities side of the Balance Sheet.

fun_activity.title: 🍰 The Charity Bake Sale
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are running a charity bake sale. You collect $100 cash (Receipt). You spent $30 on ingredients (Payment). But $20 of that cash was given in advance for next year's sale! Calculate your actual Income for THIS year to find your true Surplus.

exam_tips: 📌 Subscription Calculation is a guaranteed 3 or 4-mark question: Add 'Outstanding for Current Year' and 'Advance received Last Year'. Subtract 'Outstanding of Last Year' and 'Advance for Next Year'.
📌 Receipts and Payments A/c is a 'Real Account', while Income and Expenditure A/c is a 'Nominal Account'. This is a very common 1-mark MCQ.
📌 Life Membership Fees and Legacies (unless stated otherwise) are capitalized and go directly to the Balance Sheet, NOT the Income & Expenditure A/c.
quick_recap: ⭐ NPOs do not prepare Profit & Loss accounts; they prepare Income & Expenditure accounts.
⭐ Surplus increases the Capital Fund; Deficit decreases it.
⭐ Fund-based accounting ensures specific donations are used only for their intended purpose.
